correctness.rationale: In finite Heyting H, j=double negation is a nucleus and Reg(H)=B is a finite atomic Boolean algebra. For existential witness values u_b, E=join_b u_b and T=jE; finite atom covering gives F of at most |At B| with E <= j(join_{b in F} u_b). This is precisely Aratake Theorem 3.14 finite-witness condition (under the original function-symbol assumption), so every maximal filter is generic and Łoś holds in the specified sense. Minimizing witnesses is exactly minimum set cover of atoms beneath T by atom sets beneath j(u_b). Singleton witnesses in a k-atom Boolean algebra show sharpness. A powerset Boolean algebra with one unary predicate encodes Set Cover and proves restricted NP-completeness with standard explicit finite bitvector input. Inspected verify.py that enumerates all labeled posets of at most 4 points and all distinct witness-value families, while separately checking a 4-atom Boolean cover example. This finite replay is ancillary to the general proof.
